caption: The statistics of clustering. The left is the clustering result of AttentionInfluence, the right part is that of FineWeb-Edu Classifier.
model_annotation: The image presents two pie charts comparing the thematic clustering distributions of two different datasets or classification methods: “AttentionInfluence” on the left and “FineWeb-Edu Classifier” on the right, as referenced in the paper “AttentionInfluence Adopting Attention Head Influence for Weak-to-Strong Pretraining Data Selection.” Each chart is divided into multiple colored segments, each labeled with a topic category and a numerical count representing the number of items or documents assigned to that cluster. In the “AttentionInfluence” chart, the largest segment is “Education” (25), followed by “Health & Medicine” (22), “Science” (15), “Teaching & resources” (15), “History & Society” (23), and others such as “Diseases” (11), “Animal & Plant” (13), “Society & culture” (10), “Historical review” (7), “Events & people” (6), and several smaller categories including “Infor tech” (5), “Materials” (3), “Emerging tech” (4), “Manage” (2), and “Policy” (1). The “FineWeb-Edu Classifier” chart shows a different distribution, with “Education” as the largest segment (38), followed by “History & Society” (19), “Science & technology education” (19), “Health & Medicine” (19), “Teaching & resources” (17), “Historical review” (12), “Animal & Plant” (12), “Science” (15), “Diseases” (10), “Nutrition” (7), “Healthy education” (2), “Medical” (2), “Materials” (3), “Society & culture” (5), “Events & people” (2), “Infor tech” (3), “Emerging tech” (4), “Tech & Engineer” (8), and “Manage” (1). Both charts use distinct colors for each segment and include labels with arrows pointing to smaller slices for clarity, visually emphasizing the relative proportions of each category within the respective clustering model.
